subject: Clarigo: IRP artifacts request and package delivery coordination
messages:
From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@clarigo.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: security@clarigo.com
Date: 2026-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: IRP artifacts and timeline after auth spike

Mateo,

Quick note from Clarigo Security — we saw an auth spike on a small subset of API keys tied to our integration on 2026-09-13 between 21:05-21:28 UTC. The anomaly looks contained but we need a short package for our auditors and internal risk team:

- Incident timeline with root-cause hypothesis (redacted is fine)
- Sanitized access logs around the 20-minute window (IP + UTC timestamp + hashed user id is fine)
- Any SIG/CAIQ control mapping you can provide showing how this event maps to your detection/response controls
- Confirmation of retention and deletion steps taken for any credential material

Can you confirm whether you can: 1) provide a temporary SFTP drop for logs, or 2) share a secure Drive link and a short postmortem draft by EOD Thursday (2026-09-16)? We need the artifact bundle for a regulatory review next week.

If anything indicates wider exposure please escalate to legal and to our team immediately.

Thanks,
Lisa Chen
Head of Security, Clarigo Payments
lisa.chen@clarigo.com
+1 415 555 0198

(Attachment: clarigo_request_form_20260914.pdf - filled request form)

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@clarigo.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: IRP artifacts and timeline after auth spike

Lisa — thanks for the heads up and the clear list. We appreciate the detail. Short plan below: 

1) Acknowledge: we observed the same auth spike in our telemetry and immediately rate-limited the affected key group; no further anomalous activity since the window you provided.
2) Evidence transfer: we can stage sanitized logs to a temporary SFTP folder (recommend 7-day access). Please confirm the SFTP user you want us to provision or we can accept your SFTP credentials if you prefer.
3) Deliverables and timing: Marissa (copied) will prepare a redacted incident_timeline.csv and a zip of sanitized access logs for the 20-minute window; we'll also include a SIG->CAIQ crosswalk that highlights relevant detection and key-management controls. Target: preliminary bundle by 2026-09-16 23:59 UTC; postmortem draft within 48 hours after that if no further questions.
4) Retention: our default evidence retention for incident handoffs is 30 days on the temporary SFTP unless you request sooner. We will redact PII and hash user ids per your guidance.

Jonas will stand by to pull any additional telemetry you need for forensic review. If Clarigo Legal needs an attestation letter we can route to our legal team.

Assigning action owners: Marissa (evidence + crosswalk), Jonas (telemetry extracts), Mateo (liaison + legal escalation).

-Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Security Liaison, Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.com
(Attachment: none yet)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@clarigo.com>, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-15T17:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: IRP artifacts and timeline after auth spike

Lisa / team — following up with the evidence we can share now. Please see the bundle contents below; the files are staged on our temporary SFTP at sftp://secure-transfer.redwood-inference.com/clarigo-evidence/ (credentials emailed to lisa.chen@clarigo.com). We set the folder to expire 2026-09-23 unless you ask otherwise.

Bundle contents (sanitized/redacted where indicated):
- incident_timeline_Clarigo_20260915.csv (CSV) — per-event timeline, root-cause notes column included (redacted where necessary)
- sanitized_access_logs_20260914.zip (ZIP) — access logs for 2026-09-13 21:00–21:45 UTC; user ids hashed with salt; IPs preserved for correlation
- sig_caiq_crosswalk_v1.xlsx (XLSX) — mapping of detection/response controls to SIG/CAIQ control identifiers and evidence locations in the bundle
- postmortem_draft_link.txt — short Drive link to a draft postmortem (internal) 

A few clarifications/asks from our side:
- Please confirm (by reply) the retention window you want for the SFTP drop and any mandated redaction standards (e.g., fully remove emails vs. hash).
- If you require legal attestation, let us know the recipient and the exact wording scope; we can produce a signed cover letter.

Attachment stubs: incident_timeline_Clarigo_20260915.csv (CSV), sanitized_access_logs_20260914.zip (ZIP), sig_caiq_crosswalk_v1.xlsx (XLSX)

On Tue, Sep 14, 2026 at 9:12 AM Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@clarigo.com> wrote:

>
> Quick note from Clarigo Security — we saw an auth spike on a small subset of API keys tied to our integration on 2026-09-13 between 21:05-21:28 UTC. The anomaly looks contained but we need a short package for our auditors and internal risk team: ...

-Marissa Cole
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(Attachment: sanitized_access_logs_20260914.zip - staged on SFTP)

From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@clarigo.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: security@clarigo.com
Date: 2026-09-16T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: IRP artifacts and timeline after auth spike

Thanks — we received the SFTP credentials and the staged bundle. Preliminary review looks good. A couple of quick follow-ups: 

1) Retention: Clarigo requests the SFTP folder be available for 14 days (we will download and archive locally). Can you confirm deletion on 2026-09-30?
2) Postmortem: we'd like to schedule a 30-minute review call (recorded) to walk the timeline and the SIG/CAIQ crosswalk. Proposed slots: 2026-09-17 14:00-14:30 UTC or 2026-09-17 19:00-19:30 UTC. What works for you?
3) Attestation: please include a short attestation letter confirming logs were redacted and that no PII was retained in the bundle; PDF is fine.

Also attaching a short receipt confirmation once we finish the archive (will share after successful download).

Lisa Chen
Head of Security, Clarigo Payments
(Attachment: clarigo_receipt_confirmation.pdf - will be provided post-download)
